---
title: "Data catalog and PXWeb datasets"
description: "Search the BFS data catalog and download all or part of a dataset."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

The datasets of the
[BFS catalog](https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/catalogue.html)
(article type "Data") are available in the PXWeb API. Each dataset has a BFS
number, e.g. `px-x-1502040100_131`.

::: {.callout .callout-warning}
The PXWeb API is the API of STAT-TAB, which the BFS is replacing with the
[Swiss Stats Explorer](swiss-stats-explorer.html). Check first if your
statistic is on [stats.swiss](https://stats.swiss/). See
[Get started](introduction.html#from-stat-tab-to-the-swiss-stats-explorer).
:::

```{r}
library(BFS)
library(dplyr)
```

## Search the catalog

```{r}
catalog <- bfs_get_catalog_data(language = "en", extended_search = "student")
catalog
```

`title` searches in the titles only, `extended_search` also in the
summaries. You can filter the catalog by:

- `spatial_division`: `"Switzerland"`, `"Cantons"`, `"Districts"`,
  `"Communes"`, `"Other spatial divisions"` or `"International"`,
- `prodima`: the theme (see below),
- `publishing_year_start` and `publishing_year_end`,
- `inquiry`, `institution` or `order_nr` (BFS number).

The English and Italian catalogs have fewer datasets than the German and
French ones.

```{r}
bfs_get_catalog_data(language = "en", prodima = 900212) # Education and science
```

### The whole catalog

A catalog request returns at most `limit` results (1000 by default). To get
the whole catalog, loop over the themes. Run it only when needed and save the
result, to not overload the API:

```r
themes_prodima <- c(
  900001, 900010, 900035, 900051, 900075, 900084, 900092, 900104, 900127,
  900140, 900160, 900169, 900191, 900198, 900210, 900212, 900214, 900226,
  900239, 900257, 900269, 900276
)

catalog_all <- themes_prodima |>
  purrr::map(function(x) bfs_get_catalog_data(language = "de", prodima = x)) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  distinct()

readr::write_csv(catalog_all, "catalog_all.csv")
```

### All the metadata

`return_raw = TRUE` returns the catalog as returned by the API, with all its
metadata in nested data frames:

```{r}
catalog_raw <- bfs_get_catalog_data(language = "en", extended_search = "student", return_raw = TRUE)

as_tibble(catalog_raw$description)
```

## Download a dataset

```{r}
bfs_get_data(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", language = "en")
```

`bfs_get_data_comments()` returns the comments (footnotes) of the dataset.

## Download only part of a dataset

Large datasets can exceed the limits of the API. Select only the data you
need with `query`. First get the variables of the dataset and their values:

```{r}
metadata <- bfs_get_metadata(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", language = "en")

metadata_values <- metadata |>
  tidyr::unnest_longer(c(values, valueTexts)) |>
  select(code, text, values, valueTexts)
metadata_values
```

The query is a named list: the variable codes (`code`) as names, the value
codes (`values`) as values. `"*"` selects all the values of a variable.

```{r}
filter(metadata_values, text == "Year", valueTexts %in% c("2020/21", "2021/22"))
filter(metadata_values, text == "Level of study")

bfs_get_data(
  number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131",
  language = "en",
  query = list(
    Jahr = c("40", "41"),       # 2020/21 and 2021/22
    Studienstufe = c("2", "3"), # Master and Doctorate
    "ISCED Fach" = "0",         # Education science
    Geschlecht = "*"            # all sexes
  )
)
```

A variable not in the query is left out of the result (the data is summed up
over it), if the dataset allows it.

::: {.callout .callout-tip}
For a very large dataset, you can also download the whole PX file with
`bfs_download_asset()` and read it with the pxR package. See
[Tables and files](tables-and-files.html).
:::
